title: Money Universe
subtitle: Cash, bank money, settlement, tokenisation, stablecoins, CBDCs and Bitcoin
disclaimer: A monetary-system research map, not a ranking of currencies or investment products. Policy and legal treatment varies by jurisdiction.

nodes.label: Money
nodes.description: A monetary system coordinates units of account, payments and settlement through trusted institutional or protocol arrangements.

nodes.label: Central Bank Money
nodes.description: Money issued by a central bank, including cash and reserves, anchoring settlement in the conventional two-tier system.

nodes.label: Cash
nodes.description: Physical central bank money used by the public.

nodes.label: Central Bank Reserves
nodes.description: Central bank liabilities used by regulated institutions for interbank and wholesale settlement.

nodes.label: Commercial Bank Deposits
nodes.description: Commercial bank liabilities used extensively for day-to-day payments and redeemable at par within the banking system.

nodes.label: Payment Rails
nodes.description: Systems and networks that transmit payment instructions and coordinate settlement across participants.

nodes.label: Settlement Finality
nodes.description: Final discharge of payment obligations; central bank money is the conventional anchor for wholesale finality.

nodes.label: Cross-Border Payments
nodes.description: International payments face interoperability, correspondent banking and settlement frictions targeted by current tokenisation experiments.

nodes.label: Correspondent Banking
nodes.description: Traditional cross-border banking arrangement linking institutions through account relationships.

nodes.label: Tokenisation
nodes.description: Representation of monetary or financial claims on programmable ledgers.

nodes.label: Tokenised Central Bank Reserves
nodes.description: Tokenised representation of central bank reserves proposed/experimented with as a trusted wholesale settlement asset.

nodes.label: Tokenised Deposits
nodes.description: Commercial bank deposits represented on programmable ledgers while remaining liabilities of issuing banks.

nodes.label: Tokenised Government Bonds
nodes.description: Government securities represented on programmable ledgers; BIS work treats them as a key component of tokenised financial architecture.

nodes.label: Stablecoins
nodes.description: Privately issued digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value, commonly referenced to fiat currency.

nodes.label: Stablecoin Reserve Assets
nodes.description: Assets backing reserve-based stablecoins; their quality and liquidity influence redemption and run risk.

nodes.label: CBDC
nodes.description: Digital central bank money initiatives, with retail and wholesale designs varying by jurisdiction.

nodes.label: Bitcoin
nodes.description: Peer-to-peer electronic cash protocol using a public ledger, cryptographic authorization and proof of work rather than central-bank settlement.

nodes.label: Lightning Network
nodes.description: Bitcoin payment-channel network enabling low-cost, near-instant payments anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain.

nodes.label: Digital Wallets
nodes.description: Software or services through which users control credentials/keys and initiate transfers across digital monetary systems.

nodes.label: Exchanges / Conversion Venues
nodes.description: Venues where users convert between cryptoassets, stablecoins and fiat-denominated instruments.

nodes.label: FX / Exchange Rates
nodes.description: Conversion between monetary units; cross-border arrangements must coordinate exchange and settlement across currencies.

nodes.label: Trust & Integrity
nodes.description: Monetary arrangements depend on mechanisms that sustain par value, integrity, redemption or protocol-level validation.

nodes.label: Singleness of Money
nodes.description: Different forms of money denominated in the same unit should exchange at par; a key BIS criterion for monetary architecture.

nodes.label: Monetary Policy
nodes.description: Central banks influence financial conditions through policy rates, reserves and the monetary transmission mechanism.

nodes.label: Regulation & Financial Integrity
nodes.description: AML/CFT, prudential, disclosure and payment rules shape how new forms of money may be used at scale.
